Huna bar Chinena objects in the discussion of the rock surrounded by the sea.
Rava gives the pointed response and explains the ruling.

The related entry attributes this ordering to Rav Sherira and Tosafot.
Tosafot explicitly argue that Rav Huna died before Rav Yehudah and invoke the Succession passage in Kiddushin for Rava’s birth.

The early Rav Sheshet claim remains a bounded nonfinding. The named son and Pappa in Pesachim, and Rava giving Pappa a task in Sanhedrin, establish the contrasting later relationships in the narrative.

The time of Rabbi Elazar in the Yalkut’s closing proof remains an open question in Heilprin’s argument. The Bavli and Yalkut both give the name. The distinct first speaker pairs are documented alongside Rosh.

The scope of Heilprin’s statement about earlier scholars and newer editions needs edition collation. The digital Bavli continues to have the Rav Huna opening. Differing medieval versions are attested separately.
The direct objection at this locus is ascribed to Huna bar Yehudah. Heilprin’s related entry 1018 also questions finding the Huna bar Chinena attribution here.

The abbreviation in Heilprin remains unresolved. Eruvin 26a explicitly gives the exilarch speaking the verse. The parallel is recorded without imposing an expansion or harmonizing the compressed sequence.

The Yerushalmi clarifies the paired subjects. The compressed transition and the patronymic variant remain qualified. Jerusalem Maasrot 4:3:2 locates both subjects and Rabbi Yonah discusses the form with Rav.
